title: Chapter 1: Today is a Good Day to Throw My Life Away 1
content: I threw my life away.
And I mean really threw it away, with great force and enthusiasm.
I don't know how the life that was thrown away feels about it. Under the clear blue sky of early summer, I felt incredibly refreshed.
With my hometown gradually fading into the distance, the road ahead led to a foreign land, and all that lay before me was a dream.
As I swayed in the carriage, I glanced at the girl sitting next to me, also swaying in the carriage.

Her beautiful red hair, as if spun from flames, and her translucent white skin resembled a work of art more than anything noble, and it would be more convincing to say she looked like a finely crafted statue.
Her lips held a hint of arrogance, and her neck supported a beautiful jawline; she was a stunning girl from any angle.
However...
She was completely white, enveloped in an atmosphere like burnt ash.
Her jade-colored eyes stared blankly into space, and her lips, which could weave harsh words depending on the person, were half-open, leaking meaningless sounds.
No... that's not it.
I strained my ears.
"That damn prince, that damn prince, that damn prince..."
Oh, I shouldn't have listened closely.
Feeling a twinge of regret, I looked at the girl who continued to weave words like a curse with her half-open lips.

Her eyes, which usually radiated a strong will that could intimidate anyone, were now vacant, staring blankly into space as she spat out curses. For anyone who knew her past, it would have been an unbelievable sight.
But still, she was beautiful.
Erika Solnzali.
The daughter of one of the kingdom's prestigious marquis families, a child of sword and magic.
A genius blessed with two or three gifts from the heavens.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/VYJzcGv.jpeg
And just a few days ago, she had been sentenced to exile.
Yes, this girl was being exiled from the country.
And more than anything...
She was the reason I threw my life away.
Right now, I was eloping with this girl, Erika Solnzali.
Oh, and just to add, she was my first love.
"Well then..."

With my hometown now completely out of sight, the surroundings were nothing but vast grasslands. The road was well-maintained, and the carriage was running smoothly without much vibration. I opened the carriage door and slid over to the driver's seat.
"What the hell is this?"
The driver, a slightly plump man with a strangely fitting beard, looked at me with evident annoyance.
"Isn't it rude to interrupt someone who's in the middle of cursing their elopement partner?"
The man briefly gazed off into the distance, as if contemplating whether it was appropriate to say something.
"Normally, wouldn't you lend your chest to such an elopement partner?"
"Stop it, I'll die."
Just being in the same air as her makes my heart race.
If I touch her, I'll die.
"So, let me introduce myself."
I extended my right hand to the dubious-looking driver.
"Uh... I'm Merseja, an adventurer."
As he shook my hand in return, I introduced myself.
"I'm Shin Longdagger. You probably already know, but I'm the 'chosen' elopement partner of Erika Solnzali."
"Well, that's quite unfortunate for you," Merseja said, adjusting his grip on the reins.
"Is it?"
I found myself genuinely questioning that.

But, well, from the perspective of an ordinary person, it might indeed seem that way. Most people wouldn't throw their life away just because they were eloping with their first love, whom they had given up on. I must have had a silly grin on my face because Merseja tilted his head.
"I heard from the Prime Minister that eloping with your partner means you've essentially thrown away your life as a noble?"
The Prime Minister he mentioned was Erika Solnzali's father, the head of the Solnzali Marquis Family.
"How much did the Prime Minister tell you?"
"Just the basics. That you and the young lady would be leaving the country due to some minor noble dispute, and that it would be in the form of an elopement."
I see, so it was just the basics.
Merseja looked at me with probing eyes, as if he wanted to know more about the escort and communication role he had taken on until we reached our destination.
I suppose it was a very adventurer-like action. If he knew, he would want to hear more.

It's a long journey ahead, and if he's been hired by the Prime Minister as a communication link, there shouldn't be any problem discussing the details. In fact, the Prime Minister would likely provide more information later on.
Hmm, where should I start?
After a brief moment of hesitation, I decided to talk about myself.
"First of all, I was disowned by my father."
"Disowned, just like that? You really threw your life away."

Even though I say I threw it away, I am the second son of an extremely poor viscount family. Moreover, my older brother is competent and already works as a civil servant in the royal palace, so he’s not likely to die anytime soon.
In the worst-case scenario, I have a cute younger brother.
The life of a second son from a failing noble family isn't worth much. From a commoner's perspective, it might sound extravagant, but that's the reality.

I have no family to inherit, nor do I have a family business to manage. Given that, the future of a second son who doesn't measure up isn't promising. If I could be taken in by some count or marquis, that would be considered lucky.
"Well, that was a week ago."
"That's what you call recent?"
It's your own life we're talking about, you know? I shrugged in response to Merseja, who seemed incredulous, and continued explaining.
"Do you know about the academy that nobles attend?"
"Well, I do know about it."
I pointed to myself and then to the carriage.
"She and I were students at that academy."

Of course, Merseja looked like he was about to say, 'Well, that makes sense,' but I ignored him and continued my explanation. Personally, I appreciated his eagerness, typical of an adventurer, but as I spoke, I found the explanation becoming more enjoyable.
I wanted him to stick around a bit longer; it was so absurd it was laughable.
"It's a fairly well-known story, but the Light Priestess is currently at the academy."
"That's quite fortunate."
Merseja murmured in a serious tone.
When he introduced himself, he mentioned he was an adventurer. For an adventurer like Merseja, having the Light Priestess in their home country would indeed be a blessing.
"Thanks to that, the damage from monsters has decreased recently."
Though it means less income, he shrugged ironically, which I could tell was his true feeling, but at the same time, it was clear he genuinely felt grateful.
The Light Priestess, a person beloved by the gods.
A miracle of the gods that appears once every few decades, or a divine messenger.
In a country where the Light Priestess appears, monster damage decreases, harvests are plentiful, and just having the Light Priestess there earns respect from other countries.
Unfortunately, in my homeland, Faltarl, she hadn't appeared for over a hundred years.
"Anyway, that Light Priestess is a classmate of ours."
"Well, that's something to celebrate."
I shook my head at Merseja's words, which were merely a form of agreement.
"Unfortunately, it was not a cause for celebration at all."
"I live each day thanking the gods, you know?"
I gestured to Merseja, indicating that this wasn't the point.
"The will of the Light Priestess cannot be freely manipulated, even by the king. This is clearly stated in the laws of the kingdom."
Here comes the absurd story, I couldn't help but smile wryly.
"Even the king cannot manipulate her will. Fortunately, the Light Priestess, despite being a commoner, agreed to attend an academy for nobles. So, do you know what happens next?"
"Well, it's only natural to want to get closer to her."
I could tell Merseja was choosing his words carefully.
The academy was originally established to provide systematic military education to nobles and teach them how to behave as nobles. Now, it has become a place for noble encounters.
While there is a reason for the academy to house noble children as hostages, that's more of a bonus.
What happens when you throw a "special" Light Priestess into such a place?
"You put it quite elegantly."
"Well, that's because you're a noble, right?"
I shrugged at Merseja's probing gaze.
I doubt Merseja cares that I'm a noble. I can't imagine the Prime Minister would hire an adventurer who would be intimidated by a second son of a poor viscount family.
Is he testing me or something?
"Well, whatever. It was a terrible situation."
The usually refined and cheerful nobles, who would laugh gracefully, were now gritting their teeth and groaning, their eyes bloodshot as they desperately tried to get close to the Light Priestess.
As a low-ranking noble, I merely watched the flaming inferno from the other side.

The kingdom's princes, sons of generals, and the firstborns of high nobles, all of whom were rare classmates in recent years, turned out to be completely infatuated with the Light Priestess, which must have been quite displeasing for the noble daughters.
"But the real problem wasn't that."
I glanced back at the carriage.
She was surely still cursing.
"Erika Solnzali was a close friend of the Light Priestess."
"Isn't that a good thing?"
I shook my head at Merseja's question.
"Unfortunately, it didn't turn out that way."
Erika Solnzali had quietly taken the position of the Light Priestess's friend while the high and low nobles were trying to figure out how to get close to her, each trying to sabotage the other.
It was a remarkable feat, as swift as lightning.
So much so that it wouldn't be surprising if the nobles saw the shadow of the Prime Minister behind her.

"When Erika Solnzali, the daughter of a high noble, became friends with the Light Priestess, the uproar settled down for a moment. This was surely orchestrated by the Prime Minister, and at the right time, Erika Solnzali would introduce the Light Priestess to someone."
"I didn't think she looked like someone who could be used politically."
Hey, academy classmates, are you listening? There's a commoner here who understands the Prime Minister better than you all.
"That's exactly right. She simply became friends with the Light Priestess, that's the truth."

While gazing at the fire across the river, I viewed Erika Solnzali's profile, which I had made it my mission to observe while attending the academy. To me, she and the Light Priestess genuinely appeared to be close friends.
By the way, I had been so distracted by watching Erika's profile that my grades at the academy had plummeted like a worm writhing on the ground.
"But that wasn't the main issue. If they were just friends, there would be no need for hesitation. Let's approach the Light Priestess! But..."
"Why the hesitation there?"
Ignoring Merseja's complaint.
"The crucial point was that the Light Priestess rejected every approach."
"Huh."
Merseja's response seemed to convey that it wasn't a big deal after all.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/pgx0KWM.jpeg

"After all, she's just a commoner's daughter. Nobles who thought they could easily win her over with promises of a luxurious life, as well as those nobles genuinely attracted to the Light Priestess, were met with nothing but disappointment."
Moreover— I paused for effect, feeling the excitement build.
"The reason for her rejections was none other than Erika Solnzali."
What does that mean? Merseja's expression suggested he didn't quite understand, and I realized my buildup had fallen flat.
How strange, I thought it would lead to a big revelation.
Frustrated, I continued speaking.

"In other words, for the noble sons who wanted to get close to the Light Priestess, and for the noble daughters who were hoping to quickly see the Light Priestess paired off with someone so they could have their own chance at a good match, Erika Solnzali was a major obstacle."
After Merseja muttered a small "Hmm," the sound of the carriage rattling along the road passed by.
Did he really not understand even after all that? I was starting to respect Merseja for a different reason as time ticked by.
"Are nobles really that foolish?"
Merseja asked, rubbing his eyes as if he couldn't believe it.
"I can't believe it, but just to be sure, let me ask. Did you really get exiled for such a reason?"
That's exactly right.
I shrugged and confirmed Merseja's doubts.
"Ah, wait a second."
Merseja held the reins with one hand and raised his fingers to count.
"The Light Priestess should have been in her third year at the academy. Was this story from this year?"
I shook my head in denial.
"No, this has been the case since the beginning of her enrollment."
Merseja tilted his head.
"Surprisingly, those fools tried to eliminate Erika Solnzali by any means for three years."
All of it was in vain.
As I boasted, Merseja sighed deeply in response.
I continued my story.

"Erika Solnzali is a child of sword and magic, the daughter of a high noble, and her father is the Prime Minister of the Faltarl Kingdom. When you add her friend, the Light Priestess, who has free will... well, it was impossible to do anything with just a little scheming."
That's why those fools resorted to something far beyond mere scheming.
Images of the prince, who was infatuated with the Light Priestess, and the faces of those fools came to mind.
Every single one of them was a fool.
An irredeemable fool.
"Ah, hey?"
Merseja called out to me with a troubled expression.
"I was just hired to safely escort you and the young lady. I don't know what you plan to do, but I wasn't paid to stop you."
"Did I look that bad?"
"You looked like you were about to destroy the world."
I murmured in response, stroking my chin. I must have been clenching my jaw, as it felt tense.
Thinking about how Erika's brilliant future had been closed off made me feel, well, terrible. Let the world perish.
"So, anyway..."
As I resumed my story, Merseja nodded along. He was quite a decent guy.
"The fools, who had failed for three years, thought they only had two years left, so they devised a final large-scale scheme."
The climax of this absurd story was about to begin.
"Initially, they planned to have Erika leave the academy for a year. That was the extent of their plan. However, somewhere along the way, a bigger fool appeared who outsmarted them."
If there were a word to describe the highest level of foolishness, I would want to give it to that person.
"This fool realized that she was useful."
As I prepared to share the absurdity of what was about to come, I naturally built suspense. This time, Merseja remained silent.
"Some idiot, not only from the high nobility but even from the royal family, added a little twist to the foolish plan."
My molars ground together.
"Erika Solnzali was framed for attempting to assassinate the Light Priestess."
The prince of Faltarl, who was infatuated with the Light Priestess, and the nobles, those fools, conducted a large-scale and elaborate scheme. In the end, they were used by someone.
What began as a simple plan to have Erika leave the academy for a year quickly created a significant rift between the royal family and the Prime Minister.
If this had ended as a scandal within the palace, there might have been a way to resolve the situation.
Even if there were lingering resentments between the royal family and the Prime Minister, it could have been managed.
However, the fool who utilized the plan was one step ahead.
They involved the church.
No, it was truly a remarkable feat, especially for someone so foolish.
It goes without saying that the church views the existence of the Light Priestess as something special.
Living by the simple doctrine of saving the weak, they have no interest in worldly power, but if an assassination of the Light Priestess was plotted, they would not remain silent.
Moreover, just for planning such a scheme, the legal penalty would be nothing less than death.
"Are nobles really that foolish?"
Merseja once again voiced the obvious question.
They are foolish; it's precisely because they are foolish that they can act as nobles.

"Naturally, if a high noble's daughter were to be executed for a crime she didn't commit, it would be a disaster. Especially since the other party is the Solnzali Marquis Family. The worst-case scenario could lead to a large-scale civil war."
So— I couldn't help but smile wryly.
Come on, laugh; it's a ridiculous story, isn't it?
"Through a series of elaborate schemes, they managed to avoid Erika Solnzali's execution and instead settled for the mercy of exile."
The prince and the royal family, who had been so infatuated with the Light Priestess that their eyes were spinning, apparently pulled every string they had to avoid her execution.

The fact that they managed to avoid the death penalty with the church was a testament to the seriousness of the royal family and a miracle in itself. Erika's father, the Prime Minister, was said to have turned red in the face when he learned his daughter would be exiled. But knowing that, he had no choice but to accept it.
The one who plotted to create a rift between the royal family and the Prime Minister truly played their cards well.
"Did I choose the wrong country to be born in?" Merseja muttered, scratching his head.
"By the way, what does the Light Priestess know about this?"
"There's no way she knows."
"Well, that makes sense."
Merseja sighed, exasperated.

"If the heart of the Light Priestess becomes clouded, the kingdom will falter. Even our country's fools wouldn't have had the courage to say, 'Your friend was plotted against for assassination, so she has been exiled.'"
If the heart of the Light Priestess becomes clouded, the kingdom will falter; this is no joke, just the truth.

Countries that have forced the Light Priestess into unwanted relocations or marriages have all fallen, and some have even perished. The fact that the Light Priestess is a person beloved by the gods is no mere coincidence.
"Well then, I understand the reason for the young lady's exile, but..."
Merseja spoke in a tone that suggested he was unsure if he should continue.
"Why are you eloping with her?"
"Why do you think?"
"Why, that response is so troublesome, like a wife."
Are you perhaps not popular? Well, I'm also running down the non-popular path.

"You're such a buzzkill. Honestly, if I told the Light Priestess, 'Your friend has been plotted against for assassination, so she will be exiled,' there's no doubt her heart would cloud over. The fools should have used their heads much earlier."
"And the reasoning behind that?"
After being called a buzzkill, Merseja looked slightly hurt but quickly regained his composure and chimed in.
"Alright! Let's say Erika Solnzali eloped because she fell in love with someone of a different status! That's the ridiculous idea someone came up with."
"Are they fools?"
Merseja asked for the umpteenth time.
"I became a fool. The moment I heard that the girl I loved had to find an elopement partner within just a week, I raised my hand."
In reality, it turned out that the Prime Minister, Erika's father, and my father were friends.
As the second son of a poor viscount family, a classmate of Erika's, and the son of a trustworthy friend, I was the perfect candidate.
It's surprising that the head of a poor viscount family and the Prime Minister of a grand marquis family were friends.
Thanks to that, luck smiled upon me just a week before the plan was executed, a time when normally no decent fake elopement partner could be found.
Ah, no, this is bad.
For Erika, this was no stroke of luck at all. She lost her brilliant future despite having done nothing wrong. To call that my good fortune is unforgivable, even to myself.
"I don't know why you look like you're about to strangle yourself," Merseja said, searching for words and falling silent for a moment.
"I already know you're a fool. When I said 'fool,' I was referring to the one who came up with the plan."
Hahaha, this guy really doesn't hold back.
"Well, that's how it is. Erika Solnzali and I are eloping. Lady Light Priestess will say this after the summer vacation."
As I built up the suspense, Merseja, perhaps used to it, urged me on with a look that seemed to say, "Go ahead."
"My best friend fell in love across class lines, married her partner without permission, and eloped. So, please, Lady Priestess, pray for her future and happiness," I said.
Isn't it funny? Come on, laugh!
With just a look, I prompted Merseja, who let out a deep sigh and muttered.
"How can I laugh when you say it with that face?"
My bad.
